title: Shared drawers: Floor ticket
summary: The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
Two departments have exchanged lists of reading tags for their shared equipment shelf. Tomas is checking the lower stop before the ribbon press opens. A negative reading is a real measurement and must not be replaced by an invented zero.

The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order.

Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement sharedDrawersFloorTicket(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Set intersection. The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(n + d log d); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
